papers.title: Mechanistic Insights Into How Acupuncture Modulates Host Immunity via the Gut Microbiota-Macrophage Axis.
papers.authors: Yang T, Li M, Wu X
papers.abstract:
Acupuncture is proposed to operate within the neuro-endocrine-immune network. Its therapeutic efficacy is proposed to be partly mediated through the gut microbiota-macrophage axis. This proposal is based primarily on preclinical findings. This axis may act as a biological transducer that helps sustain systemic homeostasis1. This review synthesizes current evidence on how acupuncture may orchestrate a top-down regulation of the intestinal microenvironment through somato-vagal circuits, particularly those involving PROKR2-expressing sensory fibers.
This narrative review examined recent preclinical and clinical literature on acupuncture, gut microbiota, metabolites, and macrophage polarization. Studies were selected by relevance and expert judgment. Evidence was organized around the proposed gut microbiota-macrophage axis.
In preclinical rodent models and some human studies, acupuncture has been reported to suppress pathogens such as Proteobacteria. It may also promote symbionts like Akkermansia muciniphila and butyrate-producing taxa. Butyrate promotes anti-inflammatory M2 macrophage polarization via histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibition and G-protein-coupled receptor signaling. In rodent models, acupuncture has been shown to strengthen barrier integrity. It may upregulate tight junction proteins. It may also prevent lipopolysaccharide (LPS) translocation and suppress M1-driven cascades. These effects extend distally via the gut-lung and gut-brain axes.
It is important to note that this proposed cascade is primarily derived from preclinical rodent models, and direct evidence in humans that confirms all steps from vagal activation to macrophage reprogramming remains incomplete. Ultimately, acupuncture may serve as a potential eco-immunological therapy that restores balance between the microbiome and innate immunity. This framework provides a preliminary conceptual basis for the eventual development of personalized, biomarker-driven protocols for chronic inflammatory diseases, although this hypothesis requires rigorous causal validation.

papers.title: Novel dissolving microneedles incorporating natural carrier-free self-assembled nanoparticles synergized with electroacupuncture for diabetic wound healing.
papers.authors: Zhang J, Zeng Y, Zeng H, Huo H, Zeng M, Li M et al.
papers.abstract: Diabetic wounds (DW) are one of the most common complications of diabetes with complex pathogenesis, causing high morbidity and disability. Conventional therapies fail to resolve multiple obstacles to DW healing, urgently requiring efficient and safe novel interventions. Compounds from medicine and food homology substances have attracted widespread attention owing to their superior biosafety and diverse pharmacological activities. Herein, carrier-free APC and GQS nanoparticles were manufactured separately via self-assembly using medicine and food homology bioactive components, including astragalus polysaccharide, chlorogenic acid, quercetin, β-sitosterol, and glycyrrhizin acid. Subsequently, dissolvable APC@GQS@MNs co-loaded with APC and GQS were constructed using polyvinylpyrrolidone, hyaluronic acid, and aloe vera as matrix materials. Physicochemical characterization confirmed that APC@GQS@MNs have a well-defined conical morphology, satisfactory mechanical strength, and favorable skin penetration. The APC@GQS@MNs also enabled efficient selective scavenging of cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS), while physiological ROS were less affected. Meanwhile, APC@GQS@MNs exhibited favorable biocompatibility, reduced intracellular ROS levels, ameliorated oxidative stress-induced damage to cell proliferation, migration and tube formation, promoted M1 to M2 macrophage polarization, and effectively inhibited the growth and biofilm formation of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. In vivo results showed that APC@GQS@MNs promoted collagen deposition, re-epithelialization, and reduced local inflammatory infiltration in DW by upregulating CD31, CD163, IL-10 and suppressing iNOS, NF-κB, and TNF-α signaling. Notably, APC@GQS@MNs combined with electroacupuncture exerted synergistic effects, which further ameliorated the wound microenvironment and markedly accelerated wound healing and tissue regeneration. Such synergistic therapy modulates local wound states and inflammatory responses, laying a promising foundation for the management of DW.

papers.title: A GelMA hydrogel co-loaded with ursolic acid, ferulic acid and naringin facilitates dentin regeneration by providing a multi-component odontogenic microenvironment.
papers.authors: Che J, Yang A, Mo F, Gao Y, Li Y, Cui Y et al.
papers.abstract: Dental caries is a prevalent bacterial infectious disease, yet current clinical treatments remain limited because conventional restorative materials provide only mechanical filling and fail to induce dental tissue regeneration. Herein, we developed a composite gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) hydrogel system (Gel/UFN) co-loaded with three active components from traditional Chinese medicine, including ursolic acid (UA), ferulic acid (FA) and naringin (Nar), to remodel the carious microenvironment and promote dentin remineralization and vascularized pulp-dentin-like tissue formation. Gel/UFN showed excellent biocompatibility and favorable physicochemical and mechanical properties for dental applications, supporting adhesion and proliferation of human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs). Functionally, Gel/UFN significantly inhibited Streptococcus mutans (S. mutans) growth and biofilm formation, downregulated inflammatory cytokine expression and promoted the migration and angiogenesis of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). More importantly, Gel/UFN upregulated odontogenesis-related genes in hDPSCs, thereby enhancing odontogenic differentiation, alkaline phosphatase activity, collagen maturation and regenerative mineralization. In vivo, Gel/UFN exhibited slow degradation and sustained drug release for over 55 days. After implantation of Gel/UFN-filled dentin discs into nude mice, H&E staining demonstrated the formation of vascular structures, dentin-like mineralized tissue and cell-rich pulp-like tissue. Western blot analysis further revealed increased expression of the odontogenesis-related proteins RUNX2, DSPP, DMP1, and COL1A1 in the Gel/UFN group, providing additional protein-level evidence of its pro-odontogenic effects in vivo. These newly formed tissues were observed to cover exposed dentinal tubules on the surface of dentin disc using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Micro-CT further confirmed that dental tissue induced by Gel/UFN exhibited a higher remineralization density at the defect site, supporting enhanced dentin remineralization. Overall, Gel/UFN may serve as a promising bioactive hydrogel platform for dentin repair and vascularized pulp-dentin-like tissue formation through antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, pro-angiogenic and pro-differentiation effects.

papers.title: Effect of Kunxian capsule, a novel Tripterygium wilfordii preparation, on reducing proteinuria and slowing renal function decline in diabetic kidney disease: a 48-week randomized controlled trial.
papers.authors: Chen S, Gao Y, Liang Z, Zhang Y, Wang C, Tang Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Diabetic kidney disease (DKD), a leading cause of chronic kidney disease, remains a clinical challenge despite renin-angiotensin system blockade. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of adding Kunxian capsule to standard therapy with irbesartan in patients with DKD.
Eighty patients with DKD were randomly assigned to either the experimental group (standard therapy with irbesartan plus Kunxian capsule) or the control group (standard therapy with irbesartan) for 48 weeks. Primary outcomes included the proteinuria remission rate, degree of proteinuria reduction, and median time to remission. Secondary outcomes included the slope of eGFR decline and the incidence of renal composite hard endpoint. Safety was assessed by monitoring adverse events. This trial was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov on March 2, 2021 (No. NCT04981613).
In the intention-to-treat analysis, the experimental group had a higher proteinuria remission rate (57.50% vs. 25.00%), a shorter median time to remission (5 months vs. not reached), and a greater reduction in 24-hour urinary protein than the control group. A lower incidence of renal composite hard endpoint was observed in the experimental group (10.00% vs. 32.50%), accompanied by a slower eGFR decline. No significant differences in the incidence of adverse events were observed between the two groups. Inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate, were significantly reduced in the experimental group.
Adding Kunxian capsule to standard therapy with irbesartan improved the proteinuria remission rate and attenuated renal function decline in patients with DKD, supporting its potential as a promising adjunctive therapy.

papers.title: Neuropharmacological effects of Salvia officinalis: molecular mechanisms, preclinical evidence, and clinical potential.
papers.authors: Sabet AZ, Ahmadnia H, Shahsavari K, Khanavi M, Esfahani HM, Yazarlu O et al.
papers.abstract: Salvia officinalis (sage), a cornerstone of traditional medicine, has attracted significant scientific interest for its neuroprotective benefits. This review synthesizes evidence on the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying its potential therapeutic efficacy, which are attributed to bioactive compounds including phenolic acids (rosmarinic and caffeic acid), flavonoids, and terpenoids. Six key mechanisms have been identified. First, S. officinalis enhances cholinergic activity by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase, directly counteracting cognitive deficits in Alzheimer's disease. Second, it exerts significant antioxidant effects by neutralizing free radicals, upregulating catalase and superoxide dismutase, and reducing lipid peroxidation. Third, anti-inflammatory actions involve suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6) and inhibiting COX-2/PGE2 pathways. Fourth, S. officinalis modulates neurotrophic factors, upregulating BDNF and GDNF to support neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity. Fifth, it interacts with neurotransmitter systems-activating opioid receptors for analgesia, enhancing GABAergic activity for anxiolytic and anticonvulsant effects, and influencing serotonergic and adrenergic pathways for mood regulation. Sixth, it may reduce amyloid-beta aggregation and reduces tau hyperphosphorylation. Additionally, phytoestrogenic components may contribute to benefits against cognitive decline and mood disorders during menopause. By integrating findings from in vitro, in vivo, and clinical studies, this review provides a comprehensive overview of S. officinalis as a promising multi-target therapeutic agent for neurological and neuropsychiatric conditions, highlighting its potential as a natural alternative or complement to conventional pharmacotherapies in managing complex brain disorders.

papers.title: Characteristic Dihydrophenanthrenes from Spiranthes sinensis with Therapeutic Potential for Ischemic Stroke.
papers.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
papers.authors: Qi J, Xu L, Wang Y, Li L, Zhang G, Liu X et al.
papers.abstract: Spiranthes sinensis, known as "Panlongshen", is an edible traditional Chinese medicine, widely used in herbal teas and health-promoting foods. In this study, we investigated the neuroprotective properties of S. sinensis against ischemic stroke for the first time. Bioactivity-guided isolation yielded 19 dihydrophenanthrenes, including 9 undescribed compounds (7a/7b, 9-11, 12a/12b-13a/13b). These dihydrophenanthrenes demonstrated significant antineuroinflammatory activity against NO production in LPS-induced BV-2 microglia cells, with IC50 values ranging from 1.5 to 34.8 μM, which were greater than that of the positive drug (minocycline, IC50: 34.9 μM). Furthermore, coelonin (2) reduced inflammatory cytokines in BV-2 microglia and preserved PC12 cells' viability under oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation. Mechanistic investigations revealed that coelonin (2) exerts its antineuroinflammatory effects by targeting MAP3K7 and suppressing the NF-κB signaling cascade. In vivo, coelonin alleviated ischemic-reperfusion injury after MCAO. These findings revealed the neuroprotective and anti-ischemic stroke effects of S. sinensis and identified dihydrophenanthrenes as its key active constituents.

papers.title: Acupuncture for Cardiovascular Diseases: A Review of Clinical Efficacy, Mechanisms, and Translational Perspectives.
papers.authors: Shao Y, Li Z, Zhang J, Dou W, Lu Y, Liu B et al.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of global mortality and disability, imposing a profound societal burden. While conventional pharmacotherapy and surgical interventions are foundational, they are frequently limited by adverse effects, postoperative complications, and suboptimal long-term prognoses. Acupuncture and electroacupuncture (EA), core components of traditional Chinese medicine, have attracted growing attention as low-risk, non-invasive, neuromodulatory therapies. A growing body of clinical data suggests that acupuncture/EA may be beneficial in managing diverse CVDs, including coronary heart disease, hypertension, arrhythmias, heart failure, and myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury. Furthermore, mechanistic investigations have expanded into modern interdisciplinary fields, revealing complex regulatory networks involving central neuromodulation, intracellular signaling, cytoprotection, and the gut microbiota. This narrative review synthesizes the core clinical evidence and underlying mechanisms of acupuncture/EA in cardiovascular care. We additionally collate standardized clinical protocols, encompassing core acupoints and stimulation parameters. Finally, this paper critically examines current research limitations and outlines future translational trajectories, aiming to provide a comprehensive reference for integrating acupuncture/EA into standardized CVD prevention and treatment research.

papers.title: Near-Infrared Spectroscopy for Determination of Paeoniflorin in Paeoniae Radix Rubra of Tongtian Oral Liquid.
papers.authors: Hongliang L, Xiaoqing Z, Taiyong A, Jun W, Xinyu L, Siqi C et al.
papers.abstract: Considering the limitations of conventional high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), including lengthy analysis times and high costs, near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy combined with chemometrics was investigated as a rapid method for determining paeoniflorin in the Paeoniae Radix Rubra extract of Tongtian Oral Liquid. Three samples were acquired from each of 67 independent production batches. Each sample was measured three times by NIR spectroscopy, and the three technical measurements were averaged wavelength-by-wavelength, yielding 201 representative spectra for modeling. The paeoniflorin concentration ranged from 2.3 to 50.0 mg/mL, and spectra were collected over 908.1-1676.2 nm. Following a three-way spectrum-level split into training, validation, and test sets, 87 wavelengths with Variable Importance in Projection (VIP) > 1.0 were selected using Partial Least Squares-Variable Importance in Projection (PLS-VIP). Among seven chemometric algorithms, Lasso regression achieved the best predictive performance (test R2 = 0.9994, Root mean Square error = 1.11 mg/mL, Mean absolute error = 0.89 mg/mL, Residual Predictive Deviation = 12.4), while reducing measurement time from 30-40 min to 2-3 min and the estimated cost by 90%. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis identified several informative wavelengths and spectral regions associated with O-H and C-H absorptions. These findings demonstrate the potential of NIR-based chemometric analysis as a rapid and cost-effective approach to assessing paeoniflorin quality in traditional Chinese medicine manufacturing.

papers.title: Standardized Preparation of Ruyi Jinhuang Paste from Herbal Powder and Its Topical Application for Knee Osteoarthritis.
papers.authors: Qu Z, Gong Z, Guo T, Xiang Z, Tang K, Tan X et al.
papers.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common chronic degenerative disease with an extremely high incidence in middle-aged and elderly people, characterized by a long disease course and progressive aggravation. Knee pain, swelling, and dysfunction severely reduce patients' quality of life and constitute the major health problem in this population. Currently, western medical treatments (such as non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDs]) can relieve symptoms. However, long-term use is often accompanied by gastrointestinal and cardiovascular risks, which can hardly meet patients' needs for long-term safe management, and the recurrence rate is relatively high. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) has a long history and extensive experience in treating orthopedic diseases. As a characteristic TCM therapy, herbal topical application is a commonly used TCM nursing intervention that can be prepared and applied without complex equipment, making it potentially suitable for use outside the hospital after appropriate instruction. This paper aims to introduce a standardized method for preparing and applying herbal ointment for self-management among KOA patients, including site selection, procedural steps, treatment duration, and other key aspects.

papers.title: Qi Yin San Liang San prevents gefitinib-induced nociceptive hypersensitivity by modulating TRPV1 channel activity.
papers.authors: Yan K, Guo PX, Liang QY, Xu PT, Jin T, Chen LY et al.
papers.abstract:
Qi Yin San Liang San (QYSLS) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula used as an adjunctive therapy for malignant tumors, and has been reported to reduce treatment-related toxicities. Gefitinib-associated nociceptive hypersensitivity remains underrecognized, with its underlying causal mechanism poorly defined. It is unclear whether QYSLS can prevent gefitinib-evoked adverse effect and the underlying molecular mechanism remain unknown.
To explore the molecular mechanism of gefitinib-provoked nociceptive hypersensitivity and evaluate the preventive effects of QYSLS, with specific investigation of TRPV1 channel activity and CGRP release from dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neuron under this pathological condition.
A mouse model of gefitinib-provoked nociceptive hypersensitivity was established. QYSLS protection was assessed via pain behavioral tests and DRG histopathology. RNA-seq and network pharmacology were used for target screening. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR), cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and molecular docking confirmed direct gefitinib-TRPV1 binding. Calcium imaging evaluated TRPV1 channel activity in primary DRG neurons and TRPV1-overexpressing cells. Trpv1-/- mice were used to validate its function. RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence staining and ELISA measured DRG TRPV1/CGRP expression and CGRP release.
Gefitinib induced time-dependent declines in mechanical withdrawal thresholds (8.7% of the control at day 28) and thermal withdrawal latencies (55.3% of control at day 28), accompanied by DRG injury in mice. DRG RNA-seq revealed elevated Trpv1 transcripts levels and enrichment of ion channel pathways. Gefitinib triggered TRPV1-dependent elevation of intracellular Ca2+ signals in DRG nociceptive neurons. Calcium imaging, SPR, CETSA, molecular docking and site-directed mutagenesis showed that gefitinib directly activates TRPV1. Residue Y454 is critical for this effect, while it is dispensable for capsaicin-mediated TRPV1 activation, and this activation elicits significant Ca2+ influx, neuronal excitation, and increased CGRP in DRG neurons. Genetic deletion of Trpv1 largely restored pain thresholds and rescued gefitinib-caused neuropathic pain. Oral QYSLS alleviated gefitinib-evoked weight loss, DRG histological damage and nociceptive hypersensitivity (recovered to 50.5% of control for mechanical withdrawal thresholds, and 94.7% of control for thermal withdrawal latency at day 28), accompanied by reductions in gefitinib-triggered DRG TRPV1 and CGRP expression of ∼34.6% and ∼56.1%, respectively. Quercetin and ferulic acid, the key bioactive ingredients of QYSLS, can inhibit gefitinib-induced TRPV1 activation. The analgesic-protective effects of QYSLS were substantially blunted in Trpv1-/- mice.
This work identifies a previously unrecognized mechanism: Gefitinib triggers nociceptive hypersensitivity via DRG TRPV1 direct activation. Residue Y454 is critical for gefitinib- but not capsaicin-evoked TRPV1 activation, and CGRP may act as a downstream effector. QYSLS prevents this nociceptive hypersensitivity largely through TRPV1.

summary.limitations: 마우스 전임상 연구로 인간 환자에서의 유효성과 안전성은 직접 확인되지 않았다.

papers.title: Cycloastragenol suppresses LPS-induced macrophage inflammation and promotes M2 polarization via TLR4/NF-κB signaling and SIRT1-related regulation.
papers.authors: Zhou X, Qin S, Guo Y, Niu W, Chang X, Wang S et al.
papers.abstract:
Astragalus has long been used in traditional Chinese medicine for tonifying qi and supporting defensive functions. Cycloastragenol (CAG), a characteristic triterpenoid aglycone derived from Astragalus saponins, has emerging pharmacological relevance in immune and inflammatory regulation, but its role in macrophage inflammatory regulation and phenotypic remodeling remains insufficiently defined.
To investigate the effects of CAG on lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced macrophage inflammation and phenotypic remodeling, focusing on Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling and the involvement of sirtuin 1 (SIRT1).
RAW 264.7 macrophages were pretreated with CAG before LPS stimulation. Cytokine secretion, phenotype markers, and inflammatory signaling were evaluated by ELISA, immunofluorescence, reverse transcription quantitative PCR, and Western blotting. SIRT1-targeting small interfering RNA was used for functional evaluation. Network pharmacology prioritized candidate targets, while two acute inflammatory tissue transcriptomes and a normal human immune atlas provided expression context. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations explored candidate CAG-protein interactions.
Compared with LPS alone, CAG at 20 μmol/L reduced TNF-α from 56.15 ± 2.17 to 25.80 ± 1.87 pg/mL and IL-1β from 93.55 ± 2.66 to 44.49 ± 2.85 pg/mL (mean ± standard deviation; both Tukey-adjusted P < 0.0001). At this concentration, CAG decreased inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and CD86 and increased arginase-1 (ARG1) and CD206. Network pharmacology prioritized TLR4 and SIRT1. Wounded human skin and LPS-exposed mouse lungs showed increased expression of the gene encoding monocyte chemoattractant protein-1-induced protein 1 (MCPIP1). The human atlas detected transcripts for these regulators in macrophages and monocytes. CAG attenuated TLR4/NF-κB signaling and partially restored SIRT1 expression. During CAG treatment, SIRT1 silencing increased TLR4 expression, the phosphorylated/total p65 ratio, iNOS, and CD86 and decreased ARG1, weakening the signaling and phenotypic effects of CAG. Docking and simulations suggested possible CAG-protein interactions.
CAG attenuated LPS-induced macrophage inflammation and favored M2-associated phenotypic remodeling, with SIRT1 contributing to these effects. These findings support CAG as a promising Astragalus-derived immunomodulatory candidate and provide a basis for further exploration of its clinical translational potential.
